reader_notes: Reads as polished long-form science journalism; no self-contradictions on a careful second pass. The seaward/leeward contrast is set up early and paid off consistently.
Quotations use single quotation marks ('People have spent...') where the sibling ELF units use double quotes; purely cosmetic, but a batch-level style inconsistency a student might notice.

Q4 is answerable only by transferring the leeward-slope finding to a new site. That is a legitimate inference task, but it is the one question where a hurried reader could latch onto the seaward figure in option A.

Q2 hinges on 'on the order of two in three' vs option B's 'every ... came through'; the hedged phrasing in the passage is what makes B wrong, so the item rewards careful reading of quantifiers rather than keyword matching.
